content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed to study the quantum version of reinforcement learning, with very brief highlights of its definition, potential applications, and different architectures to implement quantum reinforcement learning algorithms.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Although the topic of quantum reinforcement learning is very interesting, this paper is a clear reject to ICLR 2023 from many perspectives.

1. I didn’t see any original research contribution made by the paper. Apart from the introduction, preliminaries, and future prospects & conclusions, the only technical section is Section 3.2, which gives a quantum DQN (by the way, the paper never explained what a DQN is). However, this is more like a showcase and direct calculation of a basic parametrized quantum circuit.

2. In general, the paper is very poorly organized. The introduction simply put together some references in reinforcement learning and quantum computing, respectively, without giving a clear storyline – in general, a paper “quantum reinforcement learning” is probably too general, and the authors may want to zoom into a specific direction or topic. Section 3 directly goes into the DQN example without further explanation. The discussions in Section 4 and 5 for future prospects and conclusion are very vague and it’s not clear to see future research proposals.

3. The paper is in general poorly written. There are typos throughout the paper. At the end, the authors directly copy down “author contributions” and “acknowledgements” sections from the latex template.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As I discussed above, the paper has no clarity, was written in poor quality, and has no novelty. Reproducibility is not applicable.
content.summary_of_the_review: In all, this paper should be rejected from ICLR 2023. The quality of this submission might not even be appropriate say for a course project, needless to say for ICLR.

content.title: Quantum reinforcement learning
content.TL;DR: A review and implementation of quantum reinforcement learning. We used QRL to train several game agents, and finally predicted and looked forward to future applications and trends.
content.abstract: With the rapid development of quantum technology, it has been confirmed that it can surpass the speed of traditional computing in some fields. Quantum advantage can also be manifested in the field of machine learning. We reviewed many current papers related to quantum reinforcement learning. We discuss in depth how quantum reinforcement learning is implemented and core techniques. quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) method is proposed by combining quantum theory and reinforcement learning (RL).The field of quantum reinforcement learning actually includes two aspects: One is use quantum properties to help reinforcement learning, the other is using reinforcement learning to help quantum circuit design. We have completed agent training for several classic games using quantum reinforcement learning methods, and the superiority and feasibility of the simulation experiments were evaluated. The QRL algorithm can be used in many aspects such as finance, industrial simulation, mechanical control, quantum communication, and quantum circuit optimization. We take a look at the field of quantum reinforcement learning and make bold predictions that many applications in the future will benefit from the development of this technology.
